method: Conservative factual derivative excerpts across final narrative, intro and rendered captions. Counts repeated substantive facts even in reflective paragraphs; excludes independent reader reflection, caveats about missing evidence, visual reconstruction limits, Ensign Peak museum/son/horse details, primary travel journal and independently documented inscription/death facts. Underlying Holland/Uchtdorf family account treated together.

segments.weekly_schedule: Later accounts remember a Monday departure before daylight, a working week in Salt Lake City, and a Friday walk home.
segments.cow_facts: In the later family account retold by Jeffrey R. Holland, a cow bolted during milking and kicked Moyle below the knee, shattering the bone. Family and friends used a door as an operating table, and the injured leg was amputated.
segments.recovery: As the wound healed, Moyle began shaping a wooden leg. The replacement included a joint for the ankle and foot. Walking hurt. He practiced inside the house, then in the yard, and eventually farther around his property, extending what he could manage a little at a time.
segments.return: In the family account, Moyle gradually regained enough strength to resume the journey to temple work. Returning meant putting his practiced hands to use again.
segments.intro: later family memories tell of the injury, patient recovery and return to temple work for which he is remembered.

segments.repeated_recovery: Learning to use it belonged to the recovery as much as making it.
